act-samuelson.value: Samuelson's 'Economics' textbook (1948) went through 19 editions and sold over 4 million copies — becoming the dominant channel through which IS-LM Keynesianism propagated to generations of economists worldwide

child-keynesian-macro.value: 'We are all Keynesians now': Friedman's phrase (Time magazine, 4 Feb 1966, in full: 'In one sense, we are all Keynesians now; in another, nobody is any longer a Keynesian') captured the paradox of the synthesis era. Nixon said 'I am now a Keynesian in economics' (NYT, 4 Jan 1971).

child-keynesian-macro.value: Post-pandemic inflation 2021-2023 and rising public debt ratios in US/China/France reignited the Keynesian vs fiscal-discipline debate. IMF World Economic Outlook October 2025 warns of worsening fiscal outlook; directs major economies toward fiscal consolidation. Debate on whether 2020-2021 demand stimulus caused inflation re-opens the stagflation-era critique.

desc-monetarism.value: Friedman's permanent-income hypothesis (1957) undermined the Keynesian consumption function (consumption depends on permanent not current income); his natural-rate address (1968) falsified the stable long-run Phillips curve trade-off. Contribution to dormancy: estimated ~0.5 share of theoretical-kill causation vs ~0.5 from the stagflation facts themselves

desc-synthesis.value: Hicks's IS-LM renunciation (1980) was itself a gatekeeping-reversal: the disowned-mediator created a 43-year propagation of a framework its own author later rejected as a classroom gadget that suppressed fundamental uncertainty

source.title: Hicks abandoned IS-LM 35 years ago — Lars P. Syll blog (citing Hicks 1980)

fe-coldwar-mccarthy.value: Tarshis 'Elements of Economics' (1947) attacked by McCarthyist groups as Marxist; university donors withheld funding; book largely withdrawn from adoption. Pushed synthesis toward Samuelson's politically-safe 1948 version

fe-covid.value: CARES Act $2.2 trillion signed 27 Mar 2020. Inflation Reduction Act ($369bn clean energy + deficit reduction) signed 16 Aug 2022. Post-pandemic inflation 2021-2023 re-opened the stagflation-era critique of demand management. As of 2025-2026, IMF advises fiscal consolidation amid rising debt ratios.

source.title: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 — Wikipedia

fe-gfc.value: G20 Washington Summit (15 Nov 2008) committed to coordinated global fiscal stimulus. China announced RMB 4 trillion (US$586bn) stimulus on 9 Nov 2008. ARRA ($787bn) signed 17 Feb 2009. These collectively ended the ~35-year Keynesian dormancy.

fe-neoliberal-turn.value: In 1968 Nixon won the US election partly on anti-inflation platform; in 1979 Thatcher won UK election implementing monetarist MTFS; in 1981 Reagan took office. By early 1980s both major English-speaking democracies had explicitly abandoned Keynesian demand-management as official doctrine

source.title: Employment Act of 1946 — Federal Reserve History

pf-multiplier-liqpref.value: Kahn's 1931 multiplier: ~0.35 contribution share as method-operator; Keynes's liquidity-preference: ~0.4 share as the key conceptual move freeing income to adjust; the synthesis (Hicks 1937) formalization: ~0.25 share as the durable pedagogical form. All estimates with low certainty.

sw-general-theory.value: ~9 years from General Theory publication (Feb 1936) to postwar institutionalization (Employment Act 1946 / Bretton Woods 1944). The Depression and WWII compressed what might otherwise have been a multi-decade academic adoption into under a decade

source.title: Employment Act of 1946 — Federal Reserve History

sw-malthus-ricardo.value: ~107 years from Malthus losing the glut debate (1820s) to the General Theory (1936). The demand-deficiency insight lay heretical for over a century before the Depression provided the external forcing needed to make it academically and politically acceptable
